editorial_thesis: The agent advantage is moving below the chat layer: typed web capabilities, explicit non-human identity, portable physical-AI skills, and accepted-artifact measurement make autonomy more usable and governable.

topic_groups.title: Agent-Native Web + DevTools
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh web-platform signal and a neglected implementation lane: structured site actions, browser debugging, and local inference are moving agent UX below the chat layer.

sources.title: WebMCP at Chrome I/O 2026
sources.why_selected: WebMCP exposes structured JavaScript functions and HTML forms so agents can call site capabilities instead of simulating clicks.
sources.usefulness: Prototype one typed action on a Buildn/client page; compare completion rate and auditability with browser automation.

sources.title: Chrome DevTools for agents
sources.why_selected: Agents can inspect console logs, network traffic, and accessibility trees for browser-side verification.
sources.usefulness: Turn visual QA into a repeatable agent check that attaches evidence to a report.

sources.title: Modern Web Guidance
sources.why_selected: Google’s preview packages accessibility, performance, security, and Baseline guidance as installable agent skills.
sources.usefulness: Use it as a second-pass checklist for generated frontends and client handoffs.

sources.title: Chrome built-in AI APIs
sources.why_selected: On-device Prompt, translation, and language APIs can remove server inference from small personalized interactions.
sources.usefulness: Test a privacy-first summarizer or content classifier on local browser hardware.

sources.title: Chrome at I/O: AI-assisted debugging
sources.why_selected: DevTools AI combines Lighthouse context, broader search, and interactive widgets for open-ended debugging.
sources.usefulness: Measure whether agent explanations shorten time-to-fix on one real page, not a synthetic demo.

topic_groups.title: Agent Identity + Incident Sharing
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Security coverage has focused on evaluation and access boundaries; today’s fresh signal shifts toward non-human identity, short-lived authority, and shared incident learning.

sources.title: CrowdStrike Agentic Identity Provider
sources.why_selected: CrowdStrike proposes cryptographically verifiable agent identities, human/workload linkage, and short-lived least-privilege access.
sources.usefulness: Map Hermes tool calls to a task identity and produce an action ledger that survives delegation.

sources.title: SAFE guidelines for cybersecurity transparency
sources.why_selected: The Open Secure AI Alliance and Linux Foundation propose a shared process for confidential AI incident and near-miss reporting.
sources.usefulness: Create a lightweight internal near-miss schema: trigger, authority, tool, impact, mitigation, regression test.

sources.title: Ory Agent Security
sources.why_selected: Ory frames agent IAM around machine-scale authentication, MCP compatibility, and fine-grained RBAC/ReBAC.
sources.usefulness: Compare an API-first policy model against current service-account assumptions in a client architecture.

sources.title: Open Secure AI Alliance RFCs
sources.why_selected: The public RFC repository makes proposed AI-security findings and control language inspectable.
sources.usefulness: Watch for a stable incident taxonomy worth importing into Buildn reviews.

sources.title: NVIDIA OpenShell
sources.why_selected: OpenShell is presented as a runtime boundary for what agents can see, touch, and do.
sources.usefulness: Run a disposable tool experiment with explicit filesystem and egress policy.

topic_groups.title: Physical AI Agent Skills
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Physical AI has been covered as simulation and models; this fresh lane earns inclusion because portable skills now connect reconstruction, data generation, simulation, training, and evaluation.

sources.title: NVIDIA Physical AI Agent Skills at CVPR
sources.why_selected: NVIDIA connects Cosmos 3 and open skills to scene reconstruction, synthetic edge cases, simulation, policy training, and evaluation.
sources.usefulness: Borrow the pipeline shape for vision QA: ingest, generate edge cases, test, compare, publish evidence.

sources.title: NVIDIA Skills catalog
sources.why_selected: A public catalog packages portable instructions for Codex, Claude Code, and other agents across physical AI, CUDA, RAG, and infrastructure.
sources.usefulness: Inspect the metadata and install one skill in a sandbox to evaluate portability and update behavior.

sources.title: GraspGen-X research
sources.why_selected: A foundation-model approach targets zero-shot grasp proposals across unfamiliar grippers and objects.
sources.usefulness: Track embodiment-generalization as a model-eval dimension for future robotics clients.

sources.title: NitroGen embodied agents
sources.why_selected: NVIDIA’s gameplay-trained embodied-agent direction uses diverse virtual interaction to seek generalization.
sources.usefulness: Use virtual-world task diversity as inspiration for synthetic regression suites.

sources.title: NVIDIA Isaac Sim
sources.why_selected: Simulation provides the controlled environment where agent-generated scenarios can be replayed and evaluated.
sources.usefulness: Prototype scenario replay only if a client has a measurable physical-world failure mode.

topic_groups.title: Research Agents + Accepted Work
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Coverage gap: move beyond agent capability announcements to evidence about throughput, supervision, costs, and the human decisions that remain non-delegated.

sources.title: Research acceleration: the view inside OpenAI
sources.why_selected: OpenAI reports median researcher agent spend above $600/day, 3.1 agent-workdays per human workday, and continued human supervision.
sources.usefulness: Use accepted artifacts—not token volume—as the unit for measuring agent leverage in Buildn delivery.

sources.title: Scientific computing in the age of agentic AI
sources.why_selected: A field report describes coding agents modernizing scientific software in genomics and other data-rich domains.
sources.usefulness: Look for client workflows where an agent can improve a testable analysis pipeline, not just write prose.

sources.title: How agents are transforming work
sources.why_selected: OpenAI’s economic research frames agents as systems for longer, more complex tasks and measures frontier productivity potential.
sources.usefulness: Translate the framing into a task inventory: duration, handoffs, verification cost, and business outcome.

sources.title: Path to Astra: critical capabilities and frontier safeguards
sources.why_selected: The report links capability progress to safeguards and argues that deployment evidence must scale with autonomy.
sources.usefulness: Add a release gate that couples new capability with tests for authority, monitoring, and rollback.

sources.title: ChatGPT agent: bridging research and action
sources.why_selected: The product pattern combines browser, code, and file actions for multi-step office workflows with editable outputs.
sources.usefulness: Use editable artifact output as the acceptance contract for research and client operations.
